title: Why Parents Want AI Out of Schools
author: Jared Hayden
content:
![Why Parents Want AI Out of
Schools](https://storage.ghost.io/c/65/af/65afbdb5-30bf-4286-acc4-9535069adb42/content/images/2026/11/GettyImages-1321277066-1-1.jpg)

This school year, the country's two largest school districts--New York City
Public Schools (NYCPS) and Los Angeles United School District (LAUSD)--made
national news when they announced one-year pauses on student-facing generative
artificial intelligence in K-12 classrooms. Given the mounting pressure by the
Trump administration and tech companies to accelerate AI and integrate it into
the [_classroom_](https://www.whitehouse.gov/edai/?ref=compactmag.com), the
moratoria were a timely backstop applauded by tech safety advocates and
educators. And they have only continued to be so. Just last week, the parents
of a thirteen-year-old girl
[_sued_](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/05/technology/ai-safety-school-
chromebooks-google-lawsuit.html?ref=compactmag.com) Google after its Gemini
chatbot--made accessible through the girl's school issued Chromebook--nearly
helped her commit suicide.

Since their enactment, however, the policies have drawn pushback from the
educational tech industry. Earlier this month, Google announced that it would
withhold its search engine from districts that restrict AI,
[_claiming_](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/03/google-responds-to-outrage-over-
removing-search-in-schools-that-ban-ai.html?ref=compactmag.com) that its
"search and AI [features] are deeply integrated." New York City Mayor Zohran
Mamdani didn't buy it, and
[_accused_](https://x.com/NYCMayor/status/2117692668213940677?ref=compactmag.com)
the company of "trying to use its monopoly power to force AI into our public
schools." Now, NYCPS and LAUSD are
[_considering_](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/18/technology/google-gemini-
ai-search-schools-nyc-la-
chicago.html?unlocked_article_code=1.RVE.gLxg.XpnU5fMGh-0k&smid=url-
share&ref=compactmag.com) parting ways with Google Search altogether.
